Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: natural-history topic cover for an ecology education website, topic 09: estimating bird abundance from large radar archives with human review.
Create one new detailed botanical and natural-history illustration, wide landscape 3:2 composition, approximately 1536 by 1024, with a genuine transparent background.

Scene: a single connected wetland lake-margin patch at dawn. Dark moss-green reeds and delicate grasses frame a quiet blue-grey pool and a low earthy shore. Beyond the water is a narrow distant far shore with a few soft trees. A small loose flock of swallow-shaped birds is leaving the reeds and spreading naturally above the lake: perhaps seven to ten small birds in different wing positions, some low over the water and some farther away. They should read as a modest natural group, not an exact census, directional diagram or tracking study. On the far shore, a very small pale round weather-radar dome on a short discreet support is present among the distant trees. It must be subordinate to the habitat and birds, recognizably a weather radar rather than a weapon, sonar array, drone or communications dish. The dome is only a distant environmental context, not an active projected beam. Do not add a notebook.

Style and medium: a richly detailed traditional natural-history illustration painted with layered watercolor and restrained opaque gouache. Fine individually painted reeds, seed heads, grasses, water ripples, stones and soft mist close to the water. Realistic habitat perspective and natural bird silhouettes. Painterly and finely observed, not a photograph or a cartoon. Match the quiet botanical finish of a detailed forest habitat plate. Palette: muted moss and olive green, umber shore, desaturated soft blue water and cool grey dawn with a very gentle warm light near the horizon.

Composition: one organic connected landscape vignette, shallow natural perspective, dawn water and reeds dominate, visually distinct from a daylight woodland-and-meadow mosaic. The perimeter of the ground, reeds and distant vegetation is irregular and ends in fine leaf tips and delicate dry-brush traces that fade directly into transparency. All around the scene is transparent alpha, including above the birds; there is no rectangular sky or white paper. No soil cross-section, slab, plinth, platform or cutaway cube. This is not a 3D block diorama, rectangular poster or infographic.

No text, numbers, letters, labels, arrows, flight tracks, migration paths, plotted rings, radar beams, confidence bands, balls, charts, diagrams, UI, logos, watermarks or frames. No correspondence between a radar mark and a bird; no claims of unique individuals or measured bird counts. This is a conceptual ecological scene, not a field record, real radar image or scientific truth.
